clue.text: British taking English newspaper on occasion in the US

parts.note: The Times, the newspaper this puzzle appears in

explanation.surface: A Briton picks up an English paper now and then while visiting America.
explanation.walkthrough: The word usually means early in British use; in American English it can mean occasionally, which the definition flags with 'in the US'.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the adverb can mean sometimes or occasionally, so it matches 'on occasion'.

clue.text: Only time for a quantity of wine?

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'there is but one'

explanation.surface: A wry question whether only a moment is allowed for drinking some wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A butt is a large cask, and as a measure it is a fixed volume of wine or beer.

clue.text: Pass across millions taken from telecast perhaps

indicators.note: taken from says the letter for millions is removed from the broadcasting word

parts.note: to transmit is to broadcast, of which a telecast is one example

explanation.surface: Someone hands over millions removed from a broadcast budget, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit as a verb means to travel over or through something, so it means to go across.

clue.text: How to refer to a man hiding away tons?

definitions.text: How to refer to a man hiding away tons?

indicators.note: hiding away says the letter for tons is put out of sight, taken away from the title

parts.words: How to refer to a man
parts.note: Mister is the title used in addressing a man

explanation.surface: A question of etiquette: what to call a man who stashes away huge amounts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a man who hides away tons of money is a hoarder.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards wealth, keeping vast sums hidden away rather than spending it.

clue.text: Many turning up lazily and impassively

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word for many is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: lots means many
idly means lazily

explanation.surface: A crowd arrives slowly, showing no emotion at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolidly describes acting calmly and without showing feeling, the same as an impassive manner.

clue.text: Old plane nearly late — the cause of serious bird strike?

definitions.text: the cause of serious bird strike?

parts.note: bus is old slang for an aircraft

indicators.note: nearly says the word for late loses its last letter

parts.note: tardy means late

explanation.surface: A vintage aircraft running behind schedule suffers a serious collision with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A bird strike is a bird hitting a plane; a very heavy bird would make a serious one.
explanation.definitionFit: The great bustard is among the heaviest flying birds, so hitting one would be a severe collision.

clue.text: What's used in certain puddings for buffet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the flour, egg and milk mixture for Yorkshire pudding and the like
second meaning: to strike repeatedly, as waves do

explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a spread of food to go with the puddings, but it is the verb meaning to pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a cooking mixture of flour, eggs and milk and a verb meaning to pound or beat.

clue.text: Cleaner splitting big increase in extra payment

indicators.note: splitting says the cleaner goes into the word for a rise, dividing it

parts.note: a surge is a sudden large rise
a char is a British word for a cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A cleaner's arrival causes a big jump in what someone has to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional fee added on top of the usual price.

clue.text: State using the euro with gold rand adopted at the outset

parts.note: and can mean with, joining two things
or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: at the outset says to take the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: first letter of rand
first letter of adopted

explanation.surface: A country is said to have taken up the euro alongside gold and the South African rand.
explanation.walkthrough: The rand is South Africa's currency, a decoy amid the money talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra, the small Pyrenean country, uses the euro as its currency though it is outside the EU.

clue.text: I'm interned, tortured when one's wanting to eat?

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A prisoner complains of torment while held, perhaps because of hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinnertime is the hour for the main meal, the time when people are hungry.

clue.text: Team initially charged games coach, say

indicators.note: initially says to take the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of team
ran, as in charged forward
sport means games

explanation.surface: A team rushed at the start of the games, with a sports coach in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a trainer in this sporting scene, but it is a long-distance bus, an example of transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a road vehicle carrying passengers, one example of a means of travel.

clue.text: Sculptor needing staff at home

parts.note: a staff is a rod or stick
in means at home

explanation.surface: An artist who needs his staff to be in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was a French artist famous for The Thinker and The Kiss.

clue.text: What goes to block army career, perhaps

parts.note: the army is one of the armed services, an example flagged by 'perhaps'
to career is to rush headlong, to charge

explanation.surface: Something set up to stop someone joining the military.
explanation.walkthrough: 'block' seems a verb meaning obstruct, but it is a block of flats; 'career' is the verb meaning rush, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat owners pay a fee to the landlord for upkeep of the building, so the money goes to the block.

clue.text: One who may discover her career's ruined

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A scientist finds out that a woman's career has been wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A researcher investigates in hopes of making new findings.

clue.text: Ravel's magical charm in need of piano

indicators.note: in need of says the charm lacks the letter for piano

parts.note: a pentangle is a five-pointed star used as a charm against evil
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: The composer Ravel's music has a magical charm but is short of a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel the French composer goes with piano, but here ravel is the verb, and the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle threads together, the same as to entangle.

clue.text: Some number using the internet are mostly with a crooked set-up?

parts.note: N is an algebraic symbol for an unspecified number
online means connected to the internet

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the word are, kept as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A number of internet users are suspected of being part of a dodgy arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is not arranged in a straight line has a bent or crooked layout.

clue.text: Imagined team getting drunk after drive

indicators.note: after says the rearranged team follows the letter for drive

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for drive, as in a street name

indicators.note: getting drunk means becoming unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A team drinking heavily after a long drive saw things that were not there.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamt is a past tense of dream, meaning fancied or pictured in the mind.

clue.text: Heavenly power, something assumed possessed by right

parts.note: a god is a divine power
a given is a fact taken for granted

explanation.surface: A divine power, taken for granted, owned as an entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A God-given right is an inherent one, held as an unquestioned entitlement.

clue.text: Eastern variety of miner moth

indicators.note: variety of says the following word appears in a different form, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An oriental kind of moth related to a mining species.
explanation.definitionFit: The ermine moth is a white, black-spotted moth named for its likeness to the fur.

clue.text: Statement by weatherman and the rest in support

indicators.note: in says the word for the rest is placed inside the word for support

parts.note: a mast is an upright support
etc, et cetera, means and the rest

explanation.surface: The weather forecaster speaks, and everything else rests on that support.
explanation.definitionFit: A metcast is a weather forecast, a meteorological broadcast or report.

clue.text: Driving force of fellows in books — protected by mother

indicators.note: protected by says what precedes is enclosed by the word for mother

parts.note: mum is mother

indicators.note: in says the fellows go inside the books

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
men means fellows

explanation.surface: Mother shields the men buried in their reading, giving them impetus.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is impetus, the drive that keeps something moving forward.

clue.text: Demanding hotel in capital

parts.note: tall as in a tall order, something hard to do
an inn is a hotel

explanation.surface: A pricey hotel in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotel' would usually be H, the radio alphabet letter; here it is a whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallinn is the capital city of Estonia.

clue.text: Restricted mixer for gin in first class

indicators.note: in says the mixer goes inside the word for excellent

parts.note: fine means excellent, first class
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in a gin and It

explanation.surface: A limited choice of tonic for gin in first-class cabins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixer' suggests tonic, but the gin and It is a cocktail with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Finite means having limits, so it is restricted rather than endless.

clue.text: Remembering part in AMND: "… a girdle round about the earth"?

definitions.text: a girdle round about the earth

parts.note: retaining as in keeping in the memory
Wall is a role played in the rustics' play in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: Recalling a role in A Midsummer Night's Dream, with Puck's line about girdling the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck says 'I'll put a girdle round about the earth'; here the girdle is a structure holding back earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a structure holds back a bank of soil, like a belt around the earth.

clue.text: Part of Switzerland invested in a currency initially of gold

indicators.note: invested in says the canton is put inside the other letters, like money placed in a fund
initially says to take the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of currency
Uri is a Swiss canton

explanation.surface: A Swiss region puts its money into a currency originally backed by gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric is an adjective for the metal, from the Latin aurum.

clue.text: Open with part of Nessun dorma

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An opera performance starts with an excerpt from Puccini's famous aria.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot, button or parcel is to unfasten it.

clue.text: Gag the man to guard against losing secrets initially

parts.note: he, the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: losing says the guarding word drops the letter that follows

parts.note: to save is to guard or protect someone against a danger

indicators.note: initially says to take the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of secrets

explanation.surface: A man is gagged to stop him giving away secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' suggests silencing, but here it is to retch.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave can mean to retch, making the throat movements of vomiting, as does to gag.

clue.text: A change of word order during reading

parts.note: in can mean during, as in 'in the night'
a reading is an interpretation, a version

explanation.surface: Swapping words around while reading aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Inversion is reversing the normal sequence of words, as in 'said he'.

clue.text: One who's stopped working on island

parts.note: re means on or about
Tiree is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A pensioner living on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiree is a person who has given up employment, usually on reaching pension age.

clue.text: Negative characters to form company? I don't find it possible

parts.note: no is a negative
C and O are the letters that spell CO, the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A grumpy refusal to join others in forming a business.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'characters to form company' as the letters C and O, written out with the word and between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a casual way of saying something cannot be done.
